text:
Jack Drury is Nashville's defensive center now, and his trip back to Denver last week with Ross Colton was a story in itself (The Denver Post). He's playing more than 17 minutes a night, up almost two over his last ten games, with five points in 17.

The points will never be the point with him. Evolving-Hockey had him taking chances away better than almost any forward last season (99th percentile) and noted he played with very strong teammates in Colorado. This year Nashville has 49% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, slightly better than without him, on a team that's usually outchanced.

His two goals came on 2.1 expected, about right. He kills penalties and blocks shots, and he's 26, a second-round pick by Carolina in 2018 who went through Sweden's Vaxjo on the way. Our projection sees about 13 goals. The number to watch is whether his line keeps holding top competition close to even.
